Hlynyany Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is categorized as demolished and overbuilt, yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' Hlynyany's Jewish community, documented from 1474, saw the ideas of Sabbatai Zvi and Jacob Frank gain followers in the early 18th century. A Hasidic court was founded here in 1850 by Yehiel Mikhl Moskovitz. In 1894 and 1895, a four-year vocational school for 200 Jewish students and a primary school were established with support from Baron Hirsch. Hlynyany's Jewish residents were deported to the ghettos of surrounding towns in November and December 1942; a few Jewish families briefly resumed living in Hlynyany between 1944 and 1946.
